title: A Night at the Jjimjilbang
description:
A weekend night with nowhere to go, so — a jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse-sauna).
Nine thousand won for the whole night. I learned to fold the towel into a 'sheep-head' hat.

Cracked a baked egg on my forehead, washed it down with sweet rice sikhye.
In the kiln room, five years of fatigue seemed to sweat right out of me.

choices.text: Sleep on the floor of the rest hall — cheaper than a motel
choices.result_text:
Slept curled up on the heated floor. The snoring uncle next to me was the BGM.

A foreign friend would gasp, 'You sleep HERE?' —
but to a Korean this is just good value. Cheaper than a motel, warmer than a spa.

choices.text: Just enjoy the eggs and sikhye and thaw out
choices.result_text:
Two baked eggs and a sikhye. Kiln room, cold pool, kiln room again.

Whoever invented this combo deserves a medal.
Walked out with my head clear — nine thousand won of meditation.

title: A Day at the Manhwa Cafe
description:
A rainy Sunday, a manhwa (comics) cafe.
Two thousand won an hour, unlimited ramyeon and drinks, a deep beanbag.

I piled up twenty volumes I'd wanted to read and sank in.
The outside world disappeared for a while.

choices.text: Camp out all day and binge the whole series
choices.result_text:
Cooked a bowl of ramyeon and read all twenty volumes.

Didn't even notice the sun set. My neck was stiff but my heart was light.
For a two-thousand-won-an-hour hideout, it was perfect.

choices.text: Read a couple, eat ramyeon, head out
choices.result_text:
Read two volumes, then made ramyeon.
Why does manhwa-cafe ramyeon taste better?
Got up around when the rain let up.

title: One Round at the Arcade
description:
An arcade in the busy district.
Pump It Up (dance pads), a basketball game, and a photo-booth.

Feed a thousand won into the coin machine and 100-won coins pour out.
— Been a while since I heard that sound.

choices.text: Stomp out one song on the dance pad — work up a sweat
choices.result_text:
A few steps in and I was already winded. A pro at the next machine glanced over.

Bad at it, still fun. This is Korean rhythm-gaming.
Got a gym session's worth of cardio for 500 won.

Taking four-cut photos alone felt awkward at first.
But the beauty filter got a laugh out of me.

Printed one for my wallet. Today's me — better than I thought.

choices.text: Just swap coins, look around, and leave
choices.result_text:
Swapped the coins back into bills and walked out.
Even just watching the noise and lights felt good. Free entertainment.

title: The Escape Room Cafe
description:
An escape-room cafe with some acquaintances.
Twenty thousand won each, sixty-minute limit. Padlocks, ciphers, a UV pen.

The door locks and the timer starts ticking down in red.
"All the clues are inside the room."

choices.text: Rack our brains to the very end
choices.result_text:
With five minutes left, the final padlock clicked open.
We all yelled. Group photo, high-fives.

Expensive, and I want to do it again. That's the spell of escape rooms.

choices.text: Burn all the hints and barely make it out
choices.result_text:
Got five hints before escaping. The staffer smiled, 'So close.'

A success that felt like a failure — but the hour of heads-together was a blast.
Never could have done it alone.
